newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Slight falls as demand improves.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Slight falls as demand improves.

text.p: Singapore light distillates fell on Tuesday on weaker overnight crude but their slide has been gradual amid improving fundamentals, traders said.
"Naphtha especially in the Far East is not so bad even though crude has dropped drastically because of the huge petrochemical demand in Japan and South Korea," a Japanese trader said.
Traders said the market was still in contango as the prompt market was still under pressure from surplus cargoes.
But from August, the market is improving as petrochemical plants in North Asia return from turnarounds.
Singapore naphtha July swaps were talked at par to August at $21.00/$21.20 per barrel, down respectively from Monday's $21.15/$21.20 and $21.10/$21.30.
In Singapore, a petrochemical company was heard seeking spot barrels of naphtha but its trader denied any spot requirements.
Traders assessed spot fob premiums around 30-40 cents per barrel over Singapore spot quotes.
Gasoline fundamentals were assessed weak to balanced and due to improve in the later part of the month when Indonesia is expected to emerge to buy to cover shortfalls caused by refinery turnarounds.
A trader said Indonesia may need to import some 500,000-600,000 barrels of gasoline for July delivery.
Other than India's tender for a late June cargo, fresh regional demand emerged in the form of Taiwan's third July reformate tender.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) issued a tender to buy 250,000-barrels of unleaded reformate for July 24-August 15 delivery to Keelung, Kaohsiung, Shalung or Taichung, which closes June 17 and is valid for two days, a company official said.
"In the last tender, the award price was not so good," the official said. "We needed two cargoes, so now we are looking for more."
CPC's last tender, awarded just last week, took only one cargo at around $24.70 per barrel, cost-and-freight (c+f) Taiwan for July 16-30 delivery, from a Dutch trader.
CPC had earlier bought a July 1-15 arrival cargo at $24.92 c+f from a U.S. major.
